data.name: Ferd
data.gender_notes: Ferd is used as a male name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from Old High German 'ferat', meaning 'brave, hardy'. The name Ferdinand is a variant, derived from the Germanic elements 'ferd' (journey) and 'nid' (knead). Ferdinand's legacy includes Ferdinand Foch, the French general who led the Allied forces to victory in World War I. The name Ferd carries the meaning “Brave, hardy” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Ferd usually hope their child will grow to embody brave, hardy and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.etymology: Ferd belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Brave, hardy.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Ferd total 6, giving a life-path number of 6. Number 6 is linked with Venus and with the qualities of responsibility, care and community.
